how.title: Three steps and you are live
how.description: No setup call, no migration project. Connect, configure, publish.

steps.title: Connect your repo
steps.description: Point Saastro at a GitHub repository. It reads what is there — no rewrite, no lock-in.

steps.title: Configure the content
steps.description: Collections, locales and forms are declared once. The editor picks them up on the next load.

steps.title: Publish
steps.description: Every push builds and deploys. Rolling back is a redeploy of the previous version.

trust.right: One place for content, forms and deploys

headline: Your site is a project.
It should be a page you edit.
statement.description: Every copy change becomes a ticket, a branch and a deploy. That is why nothing gets changed.
points: The person who writes the copy is not the person who can publish it.
So the site stays as it was launched, and the launch was a year ago.

manifesto.title: Teams that ship their own words
manifesto.description: Not an agency retainer. Not a page builder that owns your markup.
manifesto.manifesto: The repository stays yours, the content lives in your locales, and the editor is a layer on top — not a place your site gets trapped in.

items.title: You own it
items.description: Your repo, your history, your deploys. Leaving is a git clone, not a migration project.

items.title: Made to last
items.description: Zero-JS blocks, typed props and a build-time contract that fails when a section stops being editable.

compare.title: The same five decisions, made the other way around
compare.description: What you give up with a hosted builder, and what you keep here.

rows.left: Your markup lives in their database.
rows.right: Your markup lives in your repository.

rows.left: The editor decides what is possible.
rows.right: The blocks are code you can read.
It deploys to your own account.

cta.title: Put the first page up this afternoon
